description: F-CORE-037: who recorded a posting is readable. A journal entry carries no author — the actor of the operation that created it goes into the audit record at that moment and nowhere else — so `journal` and `unfinalizedEntries` reported everything about a posting except who made it. An application building separation of duties ("nobody may finalize a batch containing their own postings") therefore read the ENTIRE audit trail on every finalization and rebuilt the mapping itself: a check that scales with the age of the books rather than with the size of the batch, and an embedding reconstructing library state from a trail, which this project has already named as a bug waiting for the first change that does not pass through the screen that writes it. Reported by an embedding application as its F-29. The trail stays the single source — the author is deliberately NOT copied onto the entry, which is append-only and could therefore never correct it.

steps.comment: A second author, so the projection has to distinguish them rather than report one value for all.
And one without an actor — recorded as the system, exactly as the audit trail records it. No invention on the read side.

expect.comment: Der Urheber steht an der Buchung, nicht nur im Protokoll.
Die Projektion, die eine Funktionstrennungs-Prüfung ohnehin liest — jetzt beantwortet sie die Frage, statt sie an den Trail weiterzureichen.
